items.title: How Long Would You Wait For GE Aerospace Stock To Come Back?
items.summary: GE Aerospace (GE) stock trades at about $329.50, about 14% below the $381.22 high it set inside the past year, and most of the decline is recent. It has fallen 12.7% over the past month. In July the company raised its 2026 guidance across the board.

items.title: How Far Can JOBY Stock Fall While Its Guidance Goes Up?
items.summary: Joby Aviation (JOBY) trades near $6.82, after falling 49% over the past twelve months while the S&P 500 returned 20.5%. The company raised its full-year revenue outlook and the shares kept sliding. The market is repricing the bill that comes before the first paying passenger in one of its own aircraft.

items.title: Should You Buy Boeing Stock While It Still Loses Money On Airplanes?
items.summary: Boeing (BA) trades at $208.87, down 12.0% over the past twelve months while the S&P 500 returned 20.5%. The complaint behind it is simple: the company still loses money building airplanes. What complicates it is how fast that loss is shrinking.

items.title: Should You Care That Lockheed Martin's Buyback Effect Is Fading?
items.summary: Lockheed Martin (LMT) has spent the past three years handing its owners a slightly bigger slice of the company each year, and the arithmetic worked. Earnings per share grew faster than net income. The stock now sits well below its 52-week high, which makes the question worth asking again: is that quiet compounding still running at the speed the record suggests.

items.title: Can Commercial Aerospace Recovery Boost Teledyne's Growth?
items.summary: TDY is poised to benefit as recovering air travel fuels aircraft orders, fleet utilization and aftermarket demand for aerospace products.

items.title: Boeing paid $3.1M FAA safety fine without public disclosure
items.summary: The fine, paid in January, covered violations tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines door plug blowout and interference with safety oversight

items.title: Boeing’s $8.4 Billion Deal Is Bleeding Red Ink
items.summary: The jet maker bought Spirit AeroSystems in December, and has since uncovered large liabilities it initially hadn’t identified.

items.title: 1 Growth Stock Set to Flourishand 2 We Brush Off
items.summary: Growth is a hallmark of all great companies, but the laws of gravity eventually take hold. Those who rode the COVID boom and ensuing tech selloff in 2022 will surely remember that the market’s punishment can be swift and severe when trajectories fall.
